prompt:
A designed desktop website first viewport mockup of the BitVault landing page, landscape 16:9, 1440 by 810 pixels, photographed as a real browser window UI not a poster and not a cinematic still. This is a production website hero: HTML layout, nav bar, type block, and CTA button. Full-bleed darkroom interior as the page background, but the image IS the website, with chrome, alignment, and readable UI text.

Palette strictly: near-black #0C0B0A page ground, safelight gel red-orange #C4452D, contact-sheet paper cream #F2E6D0, stainless canister metal #9A9488. Materials: safelight gel wash, stainless developing tank, photographic contact-sheet paper, wet enamel trays as surface texture only. No crypto, no padlock icons, no cloud glyphs, no SaaS gradients, no testimonials, no Play Store badges, no prices, no star ratings.

REGION 1 — top 8% height, full width: a thin enlarger-timer navigation strip. Dark metal bar like an analog enlarger timer fascia. Left: wordmark “BitVault” in small condensed sans, cream #F2E6D0. Right: text-link or small pill “Get the APK” in safelight #C4452D. No extra nav items. Hairline rule under the bar.

REGION 2 — left 40% of the remaining hero, vertically centered: a heroic stainless steel film developing tank / film canister standing as the phone-object, three-quarter view, wet enamel sheen, #9A9488 metal, sitting in a shallow black enamel tray. Scale is large, product-hero size, occupying most of the left column. The tank IS the vault/phone metaphor: light-tight, sealed, cylindrical stainless canister with a lid. Soft safelight rim light only. No phone screenshot overlay, no lock icon.

REGION 3 — right 55% of the hero: a safelight-illuminated rectangular contact-sheet type block, cream paper #F2E6D0 with faint film-frame sprocket marks at the edges, sitting in a pool of #C4452D safelight. This is website typography, left-aligned, designed type hierarchy:
Headline in large condensed display, dark ink on the cream sheet: “The internet never sees it.”
Deck immediately below in smaller readable body: “No account. No server. No INTERNET permission. Secrets live on the phone.”
Primary CTA button below the deck: solid safelight #C4452D rectangle with cream label “Get the APK” — looks like a print you take out of the tray, a physical button in the layout, not floating caption.
Tiny supporting line under the button in muted metal type: “GitHub APK · no account · this phone only”

REGION 4 — the entire viewport is boxed by a hard black light-trap frame, thick matte #0C0B0A border like a darkroom door gasket. No window, no outside world, no leak of daylight, no seamless studio infinity. The page ends at the frame.

Visitor job must be instantly readable: this is BitVault, it stays offline, click Get the APK. Designed website UI, not a photograph of a darkroom with captions overlaid. Sharp UI text, real layout regions, first viewport only.
